Thompson Creek (across from the campground), David Thompson Highway
Lake O'Hara Road parking, Trans-Canada Highway
Interlakes parking area, Upper Kananaskis Lake
Mount Shark Road end near Mount Engadine Lodge

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: North from Trout Lake via Mt. Adams Road, Forest Road 80 and Forest Road 8040

name: North Face of the Northwest Ridge

waypoints.name: Killen Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Randle take SR 131 south and stay left on FS Road 23 for about 31 miles, then turn left on FS Road 2329 toward Takhlakh Lake and drive about 6 miles to the Killen Creek Trailhead (from Trout Lake, follow FS Road 23 north about 23 miles to the same turn). Self-issue the free wilderness permit at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams Climbing Pass is required above 7,000 ft in summer.

waypoints.name: High Camp
waypoints.note: Meadow camp at timberline on the northwest side of the mountain, below the Adams Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Hike Killen Creek Trail #113 about 3.1 miles to the Pacific Crest Trail at about 6,000 ft, cross it, and take High Camp Trail #10 about 1 mile up a rocky spur ridge, with a short exposed talus traverse at the end, to the meadow camp at about 6,900 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Adams summit
waypoints.directions: From camp, get onto the north-facing slope between the Adams Glacier and the crest of the Northwest Ridge, gaining it below the glacier's terminus to stay clear of its crevasses and moats. Steepening 40 to 45 degree neve leads through a single narrow pinch in a rock band to the ridge crest near 10,000 ft; stay off the loose crest below that point, then continue up the ridge to the summit.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground, pass the campground and continue just under 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Pioneer Ridge Trailhead, Knik River Road
Lions Bay, end of Sunset Drive North
Mount Begbie trailhead, Highway 23 south of Revelstoke

waypoints.name: Berg Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Turn north off Highway 16 at the Mount Robson Visitor Centre, about 18 km east of the Highway 5 junction near Tête Jaune Cache, onto Kinney Lake Road. Follow it about 2 km to its end, where the Berg Lake Trail starts at about 2,800 ft. Overnight trips need a backcountry permit.

waypoints.name: Kinney Lake Campground
waypoints.directions: Follow the Berg Lake Trail along the Robson River and the east shore of Kinney Lake to the campground at the head of the lake, about 7 km from the trailhead. Bikes are allowed this far.

waypoints.name: Whitehorn Campground
waypoints.directions: Continue up the valley past Kinney Lake to Whitehorn Campground, about 11 km from the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Berg Lake Campground
waypoints.directions: Climb past Emperor Falls to Berg Lake and follow its shore to Berg Lake Campground, about 19.6 km from the trailhead. The climb leaves the hiking trail here.

waypoints.name: Mount Robson Summit
waypoints.directions: From Berg Lake, go up the Mist Glacier to the foot of the ridge. The lower rock leads to the Black Towers, passed by a chimney on the left; vertical steps and close to a mile of snow gargoyles lead on to the summit.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Drive Highway 16 (the Yellowhead) to Mount Robson Provincial Park, about 90 km west of Jasper and a short way east of the Highway 5 junction near Valemount. Turn off at the Mount Robson visitor centre and follow the paved side road about 2 km to the trailhead parking lot at its end. Check the park's trail status before you go: the trail closed after flood damage in 2021 and reopened in full in 2025.

waypoints.name: Mount Robson Summit
waypoints.directions: From Berg Lake, go up the Robson Glacier to the foot of the Kain Face, then climb its snow and ice to easier slopes and the ice gargoyles below the summit.

waypoints.name: Kinney Lake Campground
waypoints.directions: Follow the Berg Lake Trail along the Robson River and the east shore of Kinney Lake to the campground at the head of the lake, about 7 km from the trailhead. Bikes are allowed this far.

waypoints.name: Ralph Forster Hut
waypoints.directions: Near Kinney Lake, leave the Berg Lake Trail on the steep, rough climbers' trail up the south side of the peak to the hut. It is exposed in places and has one short pitch of easy fifth-class rock.

waypoints.name: Mount Robson Summit
waypoints.directions: From the hut, climb about 1,400 m of ledges and short walls by the Schwartz Ledges to the summit.

waypoints.name: Berg Lake Campground

waypoints.name: Mount Robson Summit
waypoints.directions: Ford the Robson River above Berg Lake, or walk up and cross where the Robson Glacier ends, then step onto the Berg Glacier near its toe and climb the small icefall into the bowl under the face. Cross the bergschrund and climb 14 to 18 pitches of snow and ice to the Emperor Ridge and the summit.

waypoints.name: Mount Robson Summit
waypoints.directions: Near Kinney Lake, leave the Berg Lake Trail on the climbers' trail toward the toe of the Wishbone. The arête is a long ridge of loose rock, snow and ice to the summit.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Trans-Canada Highway roadside pull-out below the southwest face
Ossa Mountain trailhead, about 30 minutes from Squamish

waypoints.name: Whitney Portal
waypoints.directions: From US-395 in Lone Pine, turn west on Whitney Portal Road and drive about 13 miles to the road end at Whitney Portal, about 8,300 ft. A Mt. Whitney Zone permit is required for both day and overnight trips into the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek during the quota season.

waypoints.name: Mount Russell
waypoints.directions: Take the Mt. Whitney Trail about 0.8 mile to the unsigned North Fork of Lone Pine Creek use trail and follow it past Lower Boy Scout Lake to Upper Boy Scout Lake. Climb north up talus to the saddle between Mount Carillon and Mount Russell above Tuleinyo Lake, then follow the exposed East Arete west over the east summit to the slightly higher west summit.

waypoints.name: Bunny Flat Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-5, take the Central Mount Shasta exit into Mount Shasta city and head east on Lake Street, which becomes Everitt Memorial Highway. Follow it about 12 miles from town up the mountain to the large Bunny Flat parking area. A wilderness permit and, above 10,000 feet, a Summit Pass are required; both can be self-issued at the trailhead, along with pack-out waste bags.

waypoints.name: Mosquito Flat Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 at Tom's Place, turn south on Rock Creek Road and drive about 10 miles to the road end at Mosquito Flat, about 10,250 ft. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Bear Creek Spire
waypoints.directions: Follow the Little Lakes Valley trail south about 3.5 miles; just past a creek crossing, take the signed climbers' trail to Gem Lakes. From Gem Lakes climb up and left across talus toward Dade Lake to the base of the North Arete, then climb the arete to the summit block.

waypoints.name: Twin Lakes (Mono Village) Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 in Bridgeport, take Twin Lakes Road about 13 miles to its end at Mono Village on Upper Twin Lake, about 7,100 ft. Overnight parking is at the resort for a fee, and a Hoover Wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Matterhorn Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the Horse Creek Trail south up Horse Creek canyon past a talus field to about 9,200 ft, then take the use trail right up steep ground to a small lake on a bench. Continue up slabs to the glacier below the north side of the peak, go a short way up the East Couloir left of the arete to its base, and climb the arete to the summit ridge, trending southwest to the top.

waypoints.name: Meysan Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 in Lone Pine, turn west on Whitney Portal Road and drive about 11 miles to the signed Meysan Lakes Trailhead parking on the south side of the road, just past the Whitney Portal Campground turnoff. Parking is limited, and the trail is reached on foot through the campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Happy Isles Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive into Yosemite Valley on Hwy 41, 140 or 120 and follow Southside Drive east toward Curry Village. Private cars cannot drive to Happy Isles; park in the trailhead parking near Curry Village and walk or ride the valley shuttle to the Happy Isles stop. A park entrance fee applies, and overnight trips need a Yosemite wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Mount Clark
waypoints.directions: Hike the Mist Trail or John Muir Trail past Vernal and Nevada Falls into Little Yosemite Valley, then follow the Merced Lake trail east past Bunnell Point. Leave the trail near its high point beyond Bunnell Point and climb southeast cross-country up one of the steep drainages below Mount Clark, through forest, slabs and talus, to the broad toe of the northwest ridge, then follow the exposed class 4 arete to the summit.

waypoints.name: Tenaya Lake Northeast Shore Pullout
waypoints.directions: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to the northeast end of Tenaya Lake, between Olmsted Point and Tuolumne Meadows, and park in the pullout along the lake's northeast shore. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

waypoints.name: Tenaya Peak
waypoints.directions: Walk south through the forest and across the meadow and creek near the east end of the lake, aiming for the toe of the buttress; faint climbers' trails in the drainage just left (east) of the buttress save most of the bushwhacking. Climb the long, mostly easy buttress to the summit.

waypoints.name: Leavitt Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 at Sonora Junction, about 17 miles north of Bridgeport, turn west on CA-108 and drive about 7 miles to Leavitt Meadows Campground. Overnight hiker parking is at the lot just as you enter the campground. A Hoover Wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Tower Lake
waypoints.note: The usual camp for the climb, below Tower Pass.
waypoints.directions: Walk through the campground, cross the West Walker River on the footbridge and follow the West Walker River Trail south past Lower and Upper Piute Meadows, turning at the signed junction in Upper Piute Meadows to climb to Tower Lake.

waypoints.name: Tower Peak
waypoints.directions: From Tower Lake climb gravel, talus and grass south to Tower Pass, where the peak comes into view, and cross the basin beyond. Go up slabs beside a lingering snow patch to the northwest ridge, then leave the ridge onto its west side and traverse into the Northwest Chute, scrambling class 3 up it to the summit, about 2,250 ft above the lake.

name: Saber Ridge traverse, south to north

waypoints.name: Crescent Meadow Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Enter Sequoia National Park on Highway 198 through Three Rivers and follow the Generals Highway up to the Giant Forest Museum. Turn onto Crescent Meadow Road and drive about 2.5 miles to its end at the Crescent Meadow parking area, the start of the High Sierra Trail. A park entrance fee applies, the road is closed by snow in winter, and a wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: South Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 in Bishop, drive west on CA-168 about 15 miles and turn left on South Lake Road, then follow it about 7 miles to the road end above South Lake, about 9,800 ft. Overnight parking at the trailhead is limited and fills in summer; a wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to Tuolumne Meadows and park in the Cathedral Lakes trailhead lot beside the Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center; roadside parking at the trail's original start is not allowed. A short connector trail leads west to the Cathedral Lakes trail. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Peak
waypoints.directions: Start up the Cathedral Lakes trail (John Muir Trail) and within the first half mile branch onto the climbers' trail along Budd Creek, which stays on the west side of the creek and ends east of the Southeast Buttress after about 1,500 ft of gain. Scramble west through the trees to the base of the buttress and climb about five pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: North Lake (Piute Pass) Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 in Bishop, drive west on West Line Street (Highway 168) about 18 miles and turn right onto North Lake Road, a steep, narrow dirt road. At about 1.6 miles turn right into the hiker parking lot near the pack station, then walk about 0.6 mile up the road to the trailhead at the far end of North Lake Campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Mount Emerson
waypoints.directions: Follow the Piute Pass Trail west for about 1.4 miles. Just below Loch Leven, where the trail climbs a series of granite ramps, leave it and go cross-country northwest to the base of the southeast face, left of the Piute Crags. Climb the blocky water streak, taking the left of two cracks that split the lower face, then easier slabs above to the summit.

waypoints.name: North Lake (Piute Pass) Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 in Bishop, drive west on West Line Street (Highway 168) about 18 miles and turn right onto North Lake Road, a steep, narrow dirt road. At about 1.6 miles turn right into the hiker parking lot near the pack station, then walk about 0.6 mile up the road to the trailhead at the far end of North Lake Campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Mount Humphreys
waypoints.directions: Take the Piute Pass Trail past Loch Leven to Piute Pass, then leave the trail and go cross-country northwest across Humphreys Basin to the highest Humphreys Lake. Climb the southwest slope, most easily by the wide chute on its far left, to the broad gully that slants up and left to the notch northwest of the summit, then finish up the northwest face, with about 100 feet of easy class 4 below the top.

waypoints.name: Tenaya Lake North Parking
waypoints.directions: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to the northeast end of Tenaya Lake, between Olmsted Point and Tuolumne Meadows, and park in the lot or pullouts along the lake's northeast shore. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

waypoints.name: Whitney Portal
waypoints.directions: From US 395 in Lone Pine, turn west at the stoplight onto Whitney Portal Road and drive about 13 miles to its end at Whitney Portal. A Mount Whitney Zone permit is required for both day and overnight trips on this route, and human waste must be packed out.

waypoints.name: Mount Whitney
waypoints.directions: Start up the Whitney Trail and leave it where it crosses the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, about a mile up. Follow the climbers' path up the North Fork and over the Ebersbacher Ledges to Lower and Upper Boy Scout Lakes, then over slabs to Iceberg Lake. Climb the couloir above to the notch, then the steep final gully and face on the north side to the summit plateau.

waypoints.name: Saddlebag Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Shepherd Pass Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 in Independence, drive west on Market Street (Onion Valley Road) about 4.5 miles and turn left onto unpaved Foothill Road at the Shepherd Pass sign. Pass the stock trailhead, then turn west onto a small, rough dirt road and follow the main track to the Symmes Creek hiker trailhead. The roads are unpaved and can be rough. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Mount Williamson
waypoints.directions: Follow the Shepherd Pass Trail up Symmes Creek, over the saddle into Shepherd Creek, and on past Anvil Camp and The Pothole toward Shepherd Pass. Below the pass, leave the trail and head southeast into the Williamson Bowl, crossing its boulder fields past the lakes to the base of the west face, then climb the class 3 chute to the summit plateau.

waypoints.name: Saddlebag Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Conness
waypoints.directions: From the dam, follow use trails southwest past the old Carnegie Institute station to the north side of Alpine Lake, then climb northwest to the East Ridge and follow it west to the broad summit plateau. Cross the plateau and drop down the sandy gully marked by a large cairn, then talus, to the base of the West Ridge, and climb the ridge (about 12 pitches, mostly 4th class with moves to 5.6) back to the summit.

waypoints.name: Glacier Gorge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 36 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Beaver Meadows Entrance, then turn left onto Bear Lake Road and follow it about 8 miles to the Glacier Gorge Trailhead at about 9,200 ft. The small lot fills very early; the park shuttle also stops here. A park entrance pass is required, and in the summer season a timed-entry reservation covering Bear Lake Road.

waypoints.name: Fourth of July Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Nederland, drive south on CO 119 about 0.5 mile and turn west onto County Road 130, signed for Eldora. Continue through the town of Eldora; past the end of the pavement, stay right at the Hessie Trailhead turnoff and again at the next fork, then follow the rough dirt road about 4 more miles to the Fourth of July Trailhead at Buckingham Campground (about 10,200 ft). The road is passable to cars in summer only.

waypoints.name: South Arapaho Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the Arapaho Pass trail past the Diamond Lake junction (about 1.1 miles) to the Fourth of July Mine ruins (about 2 miles). Turn sharply back to the northeast onto the signed Arapaho Glacier trail and follow it above treeline to the saddle on the peak's southeast shoulder at about 12,700 ft, then scramble loose rocky ground past a false summit to the top.

waypoints.name: North Arapaho Peak
waypoints.directions: From South Arapaho's summit, follow the connecting ridge north, about three quarters of a mile of mostly Class 3 scrambling with a short Class 4 crux near the end, to North Arapaho's broad summit. Escape to the west side at difficulties; the east side drops to the closed glacier basin.

waypoints.name: Lawn Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 34 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Fall River Entrance. About 2.1 miles past the entrance station, turn right onto Old Fall River Road; the Lawn Lake Trailhead lot is about 0.1 mile along on the north side of the road. A park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Castle Creek Road (end of pavement)
waypoints.directions: From the roundabout on Highway 82 just west of Aspen, take Castle Creek Road south about 12.5 miles to the end of the pavement, where passenger cars park. Beyond here the road continues as Forest Road 102, a rough road suited only to high-clearance 4WD vehicles.

waypoints.name: Castle Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow Forest Road 102 about 1.3 miles to a footbridge creek crossing, then nearly 2 more miles to the Pearl Pass junction near 11,150 ft and turn right into Montezuma Basin. Walk the road to its end near 12,800 ft, climb the headwall into the upper basin, take the path to the northeast ridge crest, and follow the ridge to the summit; the final 250 ft is steep and loose.

name: East Ridge - The Citadel (Clear Creek, CO)

waypoints.name: Herman Gulch Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-70, take Exit 218 (between Georgetown and the Eisenhower Tunnel) to the north side of the highway, where the Herman Gulch Trailhead lot sits just off the exit at about 10,300 ft. The lot fills early on summer weekends.

waypoints.name: Glacier Gorge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 36 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Beaver Meadows Entrance, then turn left onto Bear Lake Road and follow it about 8 miles to the Glacier Gorge Trailhead at about 9,200 ft. The small lot fills very early; the park shuttle also stops here. A park entrance pass is required, and in the summer season a timed-entry reservation covering Bear Lake Road.

waypoints.name: Grays Peak Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-70 Exit 221 (Bakerville), cross to the south side of the interstate and take Forest Road 189 up Stevens Gulch. Stay straight at the junction after about 1 mile and continue roughly 2 more miles to the summer trailhead at about 11,280 ft. The road is rough and a good-clearance vehicle is recommended; the lot fills early on weekends.

waypoints.name: Grays Peak
waypoints.directions: Cross the bridge over Stevens Gulch creek and follow the Grays Peak Trail up the valley to the rocky flats near 12,300 ft. The trail climbs toward the east side of Grays; at the junction near 13,300 ft stay left (right goes to Torreys Peak), then switchback up the north slopes to the summit.

waypoints.name: Huron Peak Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 24 between Buena Vista and Leadville, turn west on Chaffee County Road 390 at Clear Creek Reservoir and drive about 12 miles of dirt road to the old townsite of Winfield. Continue south about 2 miles on the rough 4WD road, staying right at the junction after 0.7 mile, to the trailhead at the road end. Passenger cars park near Winfield and walk the road.

waypoints.name: Huron Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the Huron Peak trail into the forest, cross a stream after about half a mile, switchback up the slope, then head south to treeline near 11,900 ft. Cross the high basin to the east and switchback up Huron's northern slopes to the north ridge near 13,500 ft; the rockier ground between about 13,700 and 13,900 ft is the crux before the final slopes to the summit.

waypoints.name: Longs Peak Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take CO 7 south about 9 miles and turn right (west) at the sign for the Longs Peak Ranger Station and Campground, then drive about 1 mile up Longs Peak Road to the trailhead at about 9,400 ft. The lot fills well before dawn in summer; there is no entrance station here.

waypoints.name: Longs Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the Longs Peak trail through Goblins Forest and past the Jim's Grove and Chasm Lake junctions to Granite Pass, then on to the Boulder Field and up to the Keyhole on the northwest ridge. From the Keyhole, follow the painted bullseyes across the Ledges, up the Trough gully, along the exposed Narrows, and up the slabs of the Homestretch to the summit.

waypoints.name: North Mount Elbert Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 24 about 3.5 miles south of Leadville, turn west on Colorado 300 and drive 0.7 mile, turn left onto Lake County Road 11 for 1.2 miles, then turn right onto Halfmoon Creek Road. Follow the dirt road about 5 miles to the North Mount Elbert Trailhead on the left at about 10,040 ft. The parking area fills early on weekends.

waypoints.name: Mount Elbert
waypoints.directions: Hike south to join the Colorado Trail, cross a footbridge and switchback through forest for about a mile, then turn right onto the North Mount Elbert Trail. Follow it to treeline near 11,900 ft and climb the northeast ridge, which steepens and turns rocky above 13,400 ft, to the flat crest near 13,900 ft and on southwest to the summit. On descent, stay on this ridge trail rather than the East Ridge trail.

waypoints.name: Maroon Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Aspen, drive west on Highway 82 to the roundabout, turn onto Maroon Creek Road and follow it about 9.5 miles to the Maroon Lake parking area at the road end. In summer the road is closed to private vehicles during the day, so plan on a parking reservation or the shuttle from Aspen; a fee is charged at the entrance station.

waypoints.name: Pyramid Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the Crater Lake trail about 1.5 miles to the junction near 10,100 ft and turn left onto the Pyramid Peak trail, which climbs steeply to the amphitheater below the north face. Cross the rock glacier on a faint cairned path, climb about 1,000 ft of loose scree to the northeast ridge saddle near 13,000 ft, then follow cairned ledges, the green wall and the west-side gullies to the summit.

waypoints.name: Bear Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 36 to the Beaver Meadows entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park, turn left onto Bear Lake Road just past the station and drive about 9 miles to the Bear Lake parking area at the road end. A park pass is required, and in the busy season Bear Lake Road needs a timed-entry reservation; the lot fills early, and a shuttle runs from the Park and Ride about 5 miles up the road.

waypoints.name: Arrowhead
waypoints.directions: Take the connector down to the Glacier Gorge trail, turn left at the junction for Mills Lake and continue past Jewel Lake to Black Lake. Skirt the right side of the lake, climb the boulder field and grassy slopes behind it on an intermittent path, traverse left on grassy ledges toward the valley between McHenrys Peak and Arrowhead, then scramble slabs to the long ramp that angles up right and around the north side of the summit.

waypoints.name: Bear Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 36 to the Beaver Meadows entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park, turn left onto Bear Lake Road just past the station and drive about 9 miles to the Bear Lake parking area at the road end. A park pass is required, and in the busy season Bear Lake Road needs a timed-entry reservation; the lot fills early, and a shuttle runs from the Park and Ride about 5 miles up the road.

waypoints.name: Notchtop Mountain
waypoints.directions: Go counterclockwise around Bear Lake a short way and take the Fern Lake trail about 2.8 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. Drop left to Lake Helene, go counterclockwise around it and follow cairns over rock humps to the small lake below the south ridge, then climb talus and a gully to the ramp leading up right onto the ridge crest, where the roped climbing starts and spirals around the peak to the summit.

waypoints.name: Matterhorn Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Lake City, turn west on Second Street, then left onto Henson Creek Road. Near 9 miles turn right onto the rougher North Henson Creek Road, and near 11 miles reach the signed Matterhorn Creek junction, where cars without 4WD park. High-clearance 4WD vehicles can turn up the steep, rocky Matterhorn Creek road about 0.7 mile to the upper trailhead at a Forest Service gate.

waypoints.name: Wetterhorn Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the trail north about 0.75 mile to a junction near 11,200 ft and turn right, switchbacking out of the trees, then turn left onto the Wetterhorn trail near 12,000 ft. Zigzag through the rocks to the 13,100-ft saddle on the southeast ridge, follow the ridge on a faint trail left of the crest, pass right of the Prow near 13,800 ft, and go through the notch to the final Class 3 slabs to the summit.

waypoints.name: Molas Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Silverton, drive south on US 550 about 5.3 miles toward Molas Pass to the Molas Trail parking area on the left; coming from Durango it is about a mile past the top of Molas Pass on the right. The lot is reachable in a standard car.

waypoints.name: Vestal Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the Colorado Trail down about 30 switchbacks to the Animas River, cross the footbridge, walk the railroad tracks briefly and climb the Elk Creek trail to the beaver ponds near 10,000 ft. Leave the Colorado Trail there for the unmaintained climbers' trail that climbs steeply south up Vestal Creek through deadfall into Vestal Basin, then climb the long quartzite slab of Wham Ridge, the north face of Vestal Peak, to the summit.

waypoints.name: Rock of Ages Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Telluride, drive west on Highway 145 about 6 miles and turn left onto the dirt Silver Pick Road. After 4 miles turn right onto FS 622 for 2.3 miles, then turn right at the Rock of Ages sign onto FS 645 and drive 2.2 miles to the trailhead. About 1 mile up FS 645 the road fords Big Bear Creek, which is usually manageable by mid-July.

waypoints.name: Wilson Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the Wilson Mesa Trail about half a mile to the Rock of Ages Trail and climb out of Elk Creek Basin into Silver Pick Basin on old mining roads, staying on the trail across private land, then switchback up talus to the Rock of Ages saddle. Cross the loose slope east to the Wilson Peak-Gladstone saddle, traverse south-side ledges onto the southwest ridge, follow it to the false summit, downclimb into the notch and make the exposed final moves to the summit.

waypoints.name: Pass Creek Road End
waypoints.directions: From Idaho Highway 28 in the Birch Creek Valley on the east side of the Lemhi Range, turn west on the signed Pass Creek Road, north of the old Blue Dome site. After the first couple of miles the road fords Pass Creek and turns rough; stay on the main track through a gate into the national forest. It ends as jeep tracks at a small saddle with a fire ring at about 8,000 ft, where parties park.

waypoints.name: Diamond Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the old jeep track and a worn climbers' path west up grassy slopes to a saddle near 9,300 ft, then climb the steep ridge to about 10,200 ft, where it bends northwest. Around 11,000 ft a series of 10 to 30 ft rock steps is best taken close to the crest, followed by a long stretch of Class 2 and 3 scrambling on or just left of the crest to the summit.

waypoints.name: Borah Peak Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Mackay, drive US 93 north about 20 miles and turn east onto Birch Springs Road, signed for Borah Peak, between mileposts 129 and 130. Follow the gravel road about 3 miles to the trailhead and campground at about 7,400 ft. The road is fine for most passenger cars in dry weather.

waypoints.name: Borah Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' trail east from the trailhead, climbing steeply through forest onto the open southwest ridge. Follow the ridge to Chicken Out Ridge near 11,800 ft and scramble along its Class 3 crest, downclimb to the saddle beyond, which often holds snow early in the season, then climb the steep, loose upper ridge to the summit.

waypoints.name: Redfish Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Stanley, drive south on Idaho 75 about 4.3 miles and turn right on Redfish Lake Road. Follow it about 1.8 miles toward Redfish Lake Lodge to the large dirt backpackers' parking lot on the right. A free self-issued Sawtooth Wilderness permit is required.

waypoints.name: Thompson Peak
waypoints.directions: Cross the road and follow the Fishhook Creek trail 0.8 mi to the signed Marshall Lake junction, then switchback north to the ridge top and follow it northwest toward Williams Peak. Where the trail bends north, stay left on the climbers' path across the loose south flank of Williams Peak to the high lake near 9,000 ft. Scramble the headwall break nearest Thompson to the saddle, go around the west side and climb the south gully to the summit.

waypoints.name: Mystic Lake (West Rosebud) Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 at Columbus, take Montana 78 south through Absarokee, then turn right on Montana 419 and drive through Fishtail. About 1 mile past Fishtail turn left on West Rosebud Road and follow the signs for Mystic Lake to the road end beyond Emerald Lake Campground, at the Mystic Lake power plant.

waypoints.name: Granite Peak
waypoints.directions: Walk the West Rosebud Trail #19 west about 3 miles toward Mystic Lake, then turn left on the Phantom Creek Trail #17 and switchback steeply up to the Froze-to-Death Plateau near 10,000 ft. Cross the plateau southwest about 5 miles, staying north and west of Tempest Mountain, and drop about 600 ft to the Tempest-Granite saddle. Cross the snow bridge and climb the east ridge chimneys, 4th to low 5th class, to the summit.

waypoints.name: Fairy Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Bozeman, drive north on Bridger Canyon Road (Montana 86) past Bridger Bowl and over Battle Ridge Pass. Between mileposts 21 and 22 turn left on Fairy Lake Road (FS Road 74) and drive about 6 miles to the road end at Fairy Lake Campground. The road is rough and seasonally gated, and high clearance is recommended.

waypoints.name: Sacagawea Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the Sacagawea Pass trail west through forest into the open meadows below the peak. Leave the trail in the upper basin and cross talus into the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea to the slab at the foot of the east side. Climb the steep slab, stay on the crest of the rib between two gullies, and exit onto the short ridge that leads to the summit.

waypoints.name: Summit Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Highway 58 near Crescent Lake, take Forest Road 60 about 7 miles west, then continue on Forest Road 6010 about 6.5 miles west to Summit Lake. Forest Road 6010 is rough and not maintained for low-clearance vehicles; high clearance is strongly recommended.

waypoints.name: Diamond Peak
waypoints.directions: Walk north on the Pacific Crest Trail, passing the Rockpile and Marie lakes junction at about 3.1 mi. About 1.3 mi farther, at a large open rocky viewpoint, take the cairned climbers' path west steeply up through the trees. Above treeline, climb loose rock and cinder to the false summit, then follow the narrow, exposed spine about 0.4 mi north to the summit.

waypoints.name: Hurricane Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Joseph, head west on Airport Lane, which becomes Hurricane Creek Road, to the Hurricane Creek Grange. Turn left onto County Road 521, which becomes Forest Road 8205, and drive about 3.7 miles past Hurricane Creek Campground to the road-end trailhead. The road is rough and not suited to RVs. A free self-issued Eagle Cap Wilderness permit is required.

waypoints.name: Sacajawea Peak
waypoints.directions: Walk the Hurricane Creek Trail about 1.8 miles to the unsigned, unmaintained Thorp Creek trail, ford Hurricane Creek and cross the wash of Twin Creek, then climb steep switchbacks through burned forest and blowdown to Thorp Creek Meadows, the last reliable water. Continue up Thorp Creek over fell fields and talus to the east ridge and follow it to the summit.

waypoints.name: Matterhorn
waypoints.directions: Follow the crest south over gendarmes, Class 3 with moderate exposure on the spine, or bypass them lower on the west side in scree, to the summit of the Matterhorn.

waypoints.name: Pole Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Sisters, drive about 1.5 miles west on Highway 242 and turn left onto Forest Road 15. Follow it, paved at first and then washboard gravel, staying left at the Y at about 7 miles, to the road end at the Pole Creek Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Middle Sister
waypoints.directions: Follow the Pole Creek Trail about 1.5 miles, go south on the Green Lakes Trail 0.7 mile, then west on the Camp Lake Trail 1.9 miles to an unmarked climbers' path on the west side of a clearing. Climb old moraine terraces west to the Hayden Glacier, rope up for crevasses, and ascend to the col between North and Middle Sister. Climb the steep north ridge about 900 ft from the col, staying on the crest, to the summit.

waypoints.name: West Village Lodge
waypoints.directions: From Bend, follow Century Drive, which becomes the Cascade Lakes Highway, west about 22 miles to Mt. Bachelor and turn into the West Village base area parking lot.

waypoints.name: Mount Bachelor
waypoints.directions: From the West Village base area, follow the signed summit hiking trail up through the ski area, on service roads and forest trail across the ski runs, then switchback up the steep, rocky upper ridge to the summit. This is a summer hike; in winter the mountain is an operating ski area.

waypoints.name: Timberline Lodge
waypoints.directions: From US 26 just east of Government Camp, turn north on Timberline Road and drive about 6 miles to the parking lots at Timberline Lodge. Fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the climbers' register in the Wy'east Day Lodge before starting. An Oregon Sno-Park permit is required to park from November through April.

waypoints.name: Mount Hood
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' trail on the east edge of the ski runs past the Silcox Hut and the top of the Palmer lift at about 8,500 ft. Continue up the snowfield toward Crater Rock, past Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, and swing around its east side to the base of the Hogsback. Follow the snow ridge to the bergschrund, climb the Old Chute to the summit ridge, and walk east to the top.

waypoints.name: PCT trailhead, Old Santiam Wagon Road
Green Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Bend, follow the Cascade Lakes Highway west about 27 miles, past Mt. Bachelor, to the Green Lakes/Soda Creek Trailhead on the north side of the highway at Fall Creek. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a Central Cascades Wilderness permit is required for day and overnight use during the summer permit season.

waypoints.name: Santiam Pass PCT Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Sisters, follow US 20 west about 20 miles toward Santiam Pass and turn north at the signed Pacific Crest Trail trailhead, just east of the pass summit, onto the short spur road to the parking lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Three Fingered Jack
waypoints.directions: Hike north on the Pacific Crest Trail about 4.7 miles to where a cairned climbers' trail cuts right, uphill into the woods below the south shoulder. Follow it up onto open slopes to a notch on the south ridge, then scramble north along the ridge, across the exposed ledge known as the Crawl, to the short low-fifth-class chimney and the final exposed scramble to the summit.

waypoints.name: Devils Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Bend, follow the Cascade Lakes Highway west about 29 miles and turn left (south) at the sign for the Devils Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a Central Cascades Wilderness permit is required for day and overnight use during the summer permit season. Leave a second car at the Pole Creek Trailhead first.

waypoints.name: South Sister
waypoints.directions: Cross the highway and follow the South Sister climbers' trail about 1.5 miles up through forest, across a trail junction and onto the open plateau below the South Ridge. Climb the ridge on steep scree past the Lewis Glacier's moraine lake to the crater rim and follow the rim around to the summit.

waypoints.name: Middle Sister
waypoints.directions: Descend South Sister's Northwest Ridge on snow or scree and drop to the saddle with Middle Sister above Camp Lake, then climb large talus to Middle Sister's summit.

waypoints.name: North Sister
waypoints.directions: Descend north on snow or scree, steep snow or ice early in the season, along the upper edge of the Collier Glacier to the Prouty Point saddle. Climb loose slopes onto North Sister's ridge on paths that alternate between west-side ledges and the east side at gaps, cross the exposed Terrible Traverse snowfield, climb the loose Bowling Alley gully, and move up and right to the summit block.

waypoints.name: Pole Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Reverse the ridge to the Prouty Point saddle, descend the lateral moraine on the north side of the Hayden Glacier, and follow a climbers' path down beside a creek to the Pole Creek Trail. Cross Soap Creek and follow the trail past the Green Lakes junction and through the old burn to the trailhead, roughly 5 miles from the saddle.

waypoints.name: Mt. Thielsen Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From the junction of OR 138 and OR 230 near Diamond Lake, drive OR 138 north about 1.5 miles to the Mount Thielsen Trailhead and Sno-Park on the east side of the highway. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required to park, and an Oregon Sno-Park permit from November through April.

waypoints.name: Mount Thielsen
waypoints.directions: Follow the Mount Thielsen Trail east through lodgepole pine, passing the Spruce Ridge Trail junction, to its crossing of the Pacific Crest Trail. Keep climbing the west ridge on the unmarked climbers' path above timberline, over loose pumice and scree, to the base of the summit spire, then make the short, steep, exposed hand-over-hand climb to the top.

waypoints.name: Mowich Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: There is no public road to Mowich Lake: SR 165 is closed at the Fairfax Bridge south of Carbonado to vehicles, bicycles and walkers, with no detour. The lake can only be reached on foot along the Wonderland Trail from another part of the park, a multi-day walk; camping on the way needs a park wilderness permit.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: The road to Mowich Lake is closed to vehicles at the Fairfax Bridge on SR-165, which is closed to cars, bicycles and pedestrians; there is no alternate route and the park lists no other way in.

waypoints.name: Mowich Lake

The lake can only be reached on foot along the Wonderland Trail from another part of the park, a multi-day walk; camping on the way needs a park wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Lupine Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Teewinot Mountain
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' trail from the north end of the Lupine Meadows lot straight toward Teewinot and up its many steep switchbacks to the Apex near timberline. Follow the ridge past the Idol and the Worshipper to the big east face snowfield, climb it, then 3rd- and 4th-class slabs and gullies to the summit.

waypoints.name: Mount Owen
waypoints.directions: Follow the long ridge west from Teewinot toward Mount Owen. It crosses Peak 11,840 and the East Prong, each with a major downclimb on loose rock up to about 5.6, then climbs to Owen's summit, most directly by its east ridge (about 5.6).

waypoints.name: Grand Teton
waypoints.directions: Descend from Owen to the col with the Grand Teton and climb the Grand's North Ridge (5.8), the hardest climbing of the day, to the summit.

waypoints.name: Big Sandy Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Boulder on US-191 south of Pinedale, follow WY-353 southeast about 18 miles to the end of the pavement, then continue on the Big Sandy-Elkhorn Road and follow the Big Sandy signs at each junction over roughly 25 miles of washboarded gravel to Big Sandy Campground and the road-end trailhead at about 9,100 ft.

waypoints.name: Big Sandy Lake
waypoints.directions: Follow the Big Sandy Trail about 5.5 miles, gently through forest and meadows along the Big Sandy River, to Big Sandy Lake at about 9,700 ft.

waypoints.name: Climbers' trail toward Arrowhead Lake
waypoints.directions: Continue on the trail toward Jackass Pass, past North Lake. Before the trail climbs steeply again below the pass, take the cairned climbers' trail that forks left toward Arrowhead Lake.

waypoints.name: Pingora
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' trail around the west side of Arrowhead Lake and over into the Cirque of the Towers, about 8 to 8.5 miles from the trailhead. From the cirque floor take the path toward Cirque Lake, then a smaller path right to Pingora's south shoulder; 3rd-class ramps on its left side lead to the South Buttress (about four pitches, 5.6 to 5.8), the usual start of the traverse.

waypoints.name: Lupine Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Teewinot Mountain
waypoints.directions: Take the unsigned climbers' trail from the north end of the lot straight toward Teewinot, then up many steep switchbacks to the Apex near timberline. Continue up the ridge past the Idol and Worshipper towers on your left to the big east face snowfield, climb it, then scramble 3rd-class slabs and traverse left into the V-shaped gully; its 4th-class crux leads to the summit.

waypoints.name: Lupine Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Grand Teton
waypoints.directions: Hike the Lupine Meadows trail south and up the switchbacks, keeping left into Garnet Canyon at the Amphitheater Lake junction, and follow the canyon trail and boulder field to the Meadows. Climb the Middle Fork past the moraine and up the fixed-line headwall to the Lower Saddle, then ascend to the Upper Saddle and follow the Owen-Spalding route (Belly Roll, Crawl, chimneys) to the summit.

waypoints.name: Lupine Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Middle Teton
waypoints.directions: Hike the Lupine Meadows trail south and up the switchbacks, keeping left into Garnet Canyon at the Amphitheater Lake junction, and follow the canyon trail to the Meadows. Head up the South Fork of Garnet Canyon toward the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then turn north up the Southwest Couloir to the summit.
